# Lab 19.6: Data Profiling Scans

## What We Are Going to Do
Run a data profile scan on a table and read the column statistics, in standard and lightweight mode.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create a profile scan.** Open `lab19.orders → Data profile → Create data profile scan`:
   - **Scope**: entire data
   - **Sampling**: 100%
   - **Publish results to the catalog**: on

   Click **Run now**.

2. **[CLI] Create one from the CLI.** Use a region in your dataset's multi-region:

<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud dataplex datascans create data-profile users-profile --location=us-central1 \
  --data-source-resource="//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/$PROJECT_ID/datasets/lab19/tables/users"
gcloud dataplex datascans run users-profile --location=us-central1
gcloud dataplex datascans jobs list --datascan=users-profile --location=us-central1</span>
</code></pre>

3. **[Console] Read the results.** For each column: null %, distinct %, min, max, average, quartiles and top values. For example, `status` has 5 distinct values and `gender` 2.

4. **[Console] Try lightweight mode.** Create another scan with **Profiling mode: Lightweight**. It returns in seconds with fewer statistics, good for quick checks and for grounding AI agents.

5. **[Console] Use profiles to write rules.** Note any surprises (for example nulls in `shipped_at`). You will turn them into quality rules in the next lab.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Statistics | Nulls, distinct, ranges, top values |
| Modes | Standard and lightweight |
| Published | Shown on the catalog entry |
| Use | Input for data quality rules |
